content:
We need to find template that when applied retrosynthetically to target molecule (the given SMILES) reproduces the Peterson reaction: forward reaction forms C=C double bond, breaks C-Si and C-O bonds, loses ketone and trimethylsilyl groups. In retrosynthesis, we need to break C=C double bond to give a beta-hydroxy silane (with SiMe3) and a carbonyl (ketone). So template should have functional_groups_broken: C-C double bonds (since retrosynthesis breaks double bond) and functional_groups_formed: ketones and trimethylsilyl. Also bonds broken: C=C (the double bond) and maybe C-O? Actually forward breaks C-O (the beta-hydroxy) and C-Si. In retrosynthesis, we need to form those bonds, i.e., bonds formed: C-O and C-Si. So we should search with bonds_formed: maybe "C-O", "C-Si". The tool expects bond format "6-6" etc. Not sure. Could use functional groups criteria only.

We got a result with functional_groups_broken: ["trimethylsilyl"] and formed: ["C-C double bonds"] which is reverse of what we need. That template seems to be the reverse of Peterson? It shows product is alkene, reactants include carbonyl and SiMe3CH2Li etc. That seems like the forward reaction? Actually the mapped_rxn: O= C ... + LiCH2Si(C)(C)C -> alkene product. That's a Peterson elimination forward? The template is retro: product alkene, reactants carbonyl + silyl carbanion. That matches our retrosynthetic step: target alkene -> precursors carbonyl + silyl carbanion. So this template is appropriate. It has functional_groups_broken: trimethylsilyl (i.e., losing SiMe3) and formed C-C double bonds. That's exactly our retrosynthetic transformation: break SiMe3 (remove) and form double bond. But we also need to break C-O? The beta-hydroxy silane intermediate not present? However template may be okay.

Thus we need to check if this template matches our target molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id? We have template_hash but need template_id (integer). The search result includes reaction_id but not template_id. The tool expects template_id string. Maybe template_id is reaction_id? Not sure. The required output expects template_id as integer (the one used to search the database not the hash). Likely template_id corresponds to reaction_id? In earlier examples they used integer. So we can use reaction_id 1679747.
